title: Definition, pathogenesis flowchart and the causes line
guide: CKD is the net consequence of ↓ viable nephrons (fixed at birth weight, never replaced) → intraglomerular hypertension → proteinuria. GFR = viable nephrons × sn GFR: ↓ nephron number → ↑↑ sn GFR → hyperfiltration → intraglomerular hypertension → mechanical stretching — capillary (↑ pore diameter, tubulotoxic proteinuria), podocyte (local RAAS via AT-II, ↓ nephrin), mesangial cell (proliferation → GS). Mnemonic IF TA GS; TGF-β from interstitial inflammation drives IF+TA; tubulointerstitium is 85-90% of the kidney and the determinant of decline; progression becomes etiology-independent after 50% nephron loss. Causes line: DKD (m/c, worst prognosis) > CGN (and m/c) > IN > CTID > ADPKD.

title: CKD causes table: DKD, CGN, IN, CTID
guide: Rate of fall of GFR (ml/min/year): DKD 8-10, CGN 6-8, IN 4-6, CTID 2-4. Complications row: DKD ↑↑ vascular, IN ↑↑ macrovascular; CGN and CTID are '-'.

title: G and A classification (G1-G5, A1-A3)
guide: G table: G1 ≥90 (needs radiological/biochemical/histological evidence), G2 60-89, G3a 45-59, G3b 30-44, G4 15-29, G5 <15 = ESRD (uremic phase), mx dialysis. A table (ACR): A1 ≤30 normal, A2 30-300 moderately ↑, A3 >300 severely ↑↑.

title: Complications of CKD: the ABCDE mnemonic
guide: A — anemia (unfit for transplant, ↓ GFR independently), metabolic acidosis (↓ cardiac function), access for dialysis; B — BP, bone mineral disease (renal osteodystrophy); C — cardiac (m/c cause of death): LVH → HFpEF, calcification → unfit for transplant; D — dry weight; E — electrolyte (Ca²⁺, PO₄³⁺, K⁺); U — uremic symptoms.

title: Diagnosis and the five reversible causes
guide: Diagnosis: B/L contracted kidney; diabetic nephropathy = proteinuria, edema, hypertension, retinopathy (all of); biopsy looks for IF/TA/GS. Address reversible causes: 1 obstruction, 2 drugs/toxins/alternate medicines, 3 uncontrolled hypertension, 4 ECF volume ↓ (diuretic excess, ↓ albumin), 5 hypercalcemia (nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, afferent arteriole vasoconstriction).

title: Protocol: transplant hurdles, mortality graph, dialysis indications and access
guide: Protocol starts with confirming CKD diagnosis. Transplant fit: hurdles = vascular complications (medial calcifications) → ↓ success; success ranking CGN, CTID > DKD, IN. Dialysis-mortality co-relation: mortality rate highest in the first 30 days (≈34% at day 15-50 in age >65, ≈22% all patients, ≈6-7% age <65) and falls over 360 days. Dialysis indications: uremic symptoms (definitive); volume, K⁺, acidosis (relative). Access: AV fistula, 6 weeks to mature.

title: Variation of GFR with plasma concentration (curves A, B, C)
guide: Two zones: overt renal failure (<25% GFR) and zone of compensation. Curve A — creatinine, urea, uric acid: depend largely on GFR, inverse relation. Curve B — PO₄, uric acid, K, H: rise only in late CKD via tubular secretion/decreased reabsorption. Curve C — sodium: normal throughout CRF because Na excretion per surviving nephron increases.

title: KDIGO 23 holistic approach: lifestyle, BP, proteinuria, LDL
guide: Holistic approach is first line. Lifestyle: salt 2-3 g/day, activity, stop tobacco, weight management, risk-factor reassessment every 3-6 months. First-line drugs: proteinuria — ACE(-)/ARBs + SGLT2i (curb ↓GFR), 2nd line finerenone (nonsteroidal aldosterone antagonist); BP <120/80 mmHg with 24-hr ambulatory monitoring, ACE(-)/ARB or aliskiren (never combined with ACE(-)/ARB), non-DHP CCB; LDL <100 mg/dl — rosuvastatin 20 mg/kg. LDL targets: CKD 100, diabetic CKD 70, diabetic CKD with prior CVD 55. ACE(-) C/I: pregnancy, B/L or unilateral RAS, Cr ↑>30% or K+ >5.5 after starting, hereditary angioedema.
